object: offering table (altar) found in the sand in front of the foundations of a stone mastaba
site: Wadi es-Sabu', Firth's Meroitic cemetery 150 near the Ramesside temple
notes: Permitted for publication by C. M. Firth; Pls. VIII, IX. Griffith prints seven type lines without line numbers, three in the left column and four at the head of the right, and renders the first four: 'The honoured lady (?) Mitashalbe, born of Abêsañye, kin of the chief zakaratri, lady (?) of Malañte.' 'There follow the invocation and the formulae A G' (woSi : Soreyi, then aOmXe (printed without a word space) ..., then aTtx ...). The first word (kdiqo) occurs similarly in Kar. 61; zakaratri (dkrtri) is a title in Kar.; Malañ may be a place-name and Malañte 'the (chief) in Malañ'. The X of lXl and of the formula words is the pointed form, checked at 2.5x beside the table's m, X and s.
